en: “If you are a hero and a lion,
Your first ancestor was Tügöl Khan,
Blessed from the beginning by Khydyr,
Descendant of the primal hero,
Heir to the first holy man.
Sarybay was your enemy;
Do not regard everyone as a foe.
Sarybay was the swine,
So, hero, do not cast your terrible venom upon us.
Hero, you need living souls to tend,
And a hero such as you
Needs a people such as us.
We shall sell our coursers and pay tribute;
Sarybay was the one you opposed.
If you seek vengeance upon Sarybay,
Descendant of the blessed lion,
If you charge in wrath,
Draw your sword from its sheath
And unleash your dreadful fury.
Slaughter us all.
If your daily rage seizes you,
Gouge out our eyes in vengeance.
We are Sarybay’s countless host,
A people ravaged by war.
Here and now,
We are sheep fallen into your hands.
We turn our warhorses’ heads,
Hoping you will shelter us like a poplar.
Here in front of you, Changdayak and all,
We stand with folded hands.
We are captives in your hands,
All of us accounted guilty.
If you are truly a khan,
Do not assail our precious lives,
But let us go safe and sound.
Sire, since you are our khan,
Draw your sword from its sheath.
Without sparing a single soul,
Slaughter us all.
If you ask of former times,
We are men from the Windy Pass;
Beginning struggle, conflict, and strife,
Hero, we came here to fight.
But now, brave Seytek,
We are mortals fallen into your hands.
We bow our heads to truth,
Hoping mercy will come from the hero,
And ask you for one spoonful of blood,
Too little even to fill your mouth.
As a seven-day trust,
Hero, we beg you for our lives.
If you spare us and leave us alive,
Our poplar trees will become standards,
Our knives will be whetted,
Whatever we gain we shall share together,
Companions sharing every endeavor.
Our red tongues speak eloquently;
You, river-maned lion, must decide.
Look with favor upon the innocent people.
If a gathered nation flees,
Its abandoned livestock rots at bare stakes,
Yet while it endures, a people sustains life.
The guilt for this conflict is upon my hands;
Now, gray-maned lion, we stand
In your hands, my hero.
We lie within the iron cage
Of the iron-armored gray-maned lion.
Having encountered the bloodstained warrior,
Hero, we stand within your grasp.
We have entered the flames of hell
And stand amid its embers.
From your fathers and forefathers
None ever yielded to an enemy,
No mortal who faced them prevailed,
No man could withstand their coming.
They say fortune favors the worthy,
Yet when you look within,
They say the face of the earth is broad.
How many have come lamenting,
How much wealth is there,
How much lies in the treasury?
Every soul begs for its spoonful of blood;
Understand this, noble gray-maned lion.
We are captives fallen into your hands;
I renounce defiance—hero, heed my words.
Your first ancestor was Manas Khan,
Whose yurt walls were anointed with fat.
When men such as us fell into his hands,
He made them khans throughout the lands.
He enriched the lattice walls of their yurts,
And when they fell to him as plunder,
Your champion ancestor Manas Khan
Made them khans throughout the lands.
If you are a hero and a lion,
If you are Manas’s heir in times of trial,
May you spare us,
The common folk now in your hands.
If surging wrath seizes you,
You may slaughter us all.
You will come upon us without turning aside;
If your fierce fury begins,
Then commence the massacre.
A hero needs a people;
Leave our lives intact,
Hero, act according to your will.
Livestock and souls need land,
And you, hero, need a people,
A broad nation of common folk.
Know that this is what I say;
Generous sultan, heed my words.
Heed them and leave us alive;
If you do not, slaughter us.
We stand with lives held in trust,
Amid the embers of your judgment;
If you fire your gun, we are your bullets,
If you kindle a blaze, we are your fire.
Amid conflict and calamity,
We are trapped upon the road,
In a net from which no struggling frees us.
We are in so deep a pit, hero,
That no winged creature could escape.
We are in such a broad abyss
That no four-footed beast could cross.
Having cast down our spears and bowed,
We are steeds come before you,
Regard us as strangers taken in plunder,
And ask how much wealth we possess.
Following the custom inherited from our fathers,
Let us camp together as neighboring clans,
Breaking and sharing white wheaten bread,
Joining hands upon the sacred oath,
Making our pledge firm,
Swearing upon our mortal lives,
Let us camp together as neighboring clans,
And become acknowledged kinsmen.
Let us bind our spears together;
If disaster or conflict arises,
If many treacherous foes appear,
Let us unite our strength in one place
And fight the enemy together.
Let us camp nearby as neighbors
And become kindred clans.
Let us wash our soiled linen together,
And tie the umbilical cord together.
Let us unite as one
And become mighty steeds.
Let us remain neighboring households
And become kinsmen.
Binding our spears together,
Fighting our enemies together,
Pursuing our claims together,
And scouting the land together.
The Chinese stand beyond the ridge,
Firearms confront us ahead,
And many enemies seek to attack.
If we do not die, we shall see joyful days;
If we remain alive, for you
We shall serve as a protecting host.
For you we are beyond counting;
With twelve tails and forty sweeping plumes,
We shall be wings upon your flanks.
If you carefully heed my words
And look into my eyes,
If you rule over me,
When you journey, we shall be your road;
When you enter battle, we shall be your glory.
If you enter the cold, we shall keep you warm,
A coat with silken ties and copper sleeves,
Your robe that shields you from the cold.
If you seek shelter, we shall be your haven;
If you keep and nurture us, my hero,
We shall be sweet provisions in your treasury.
When you climb upward, we shall support you;
If you spare us and make us your people,
We shall be your closest aid.
An inexhaustible store, however much you consume,
A vast treasury and great inheritance,
We are what you need.
If you lay us before you, we shall be a white road;
If we walk beneath you, we shall be a great inheritance.
We are a countless host of mighty presence;
Hero, leave us alive and put us to the test.
An inexhaustible store, however much you consume,
We are a broad treasury and inheritance.
Shaking our heads like wretched men,
We stand within your hands.
If you slaughter us, we last but one day;
If you spare us, we shall last a thousand years.
Hero, we are a great treasury and inheritance.
If we live, we shall repay your salt
And perform your service.
Hero, we are the richest treasure and inheritance;
If you raise us, we shall be your banner.
We are useful captives taken as spoils,
Steel rarely found even by master smiths,
We shall hone ourselves like black steel.
If you discipline this people,
We shall be fledgling gray hawks
That no mountain wolf can withstand.
We are sweet-tongued nightingales
Singing beneath your blessed fortune.
We are keen-eyed falcons
Preening upon your perch.
If we live, we shall gather together;
If we die, we shall share the same faith.
When we camp, we shall share the same land;
While alive, we shall remain together,
Kinsmen brought together by fate.
Hoping you will not quarrel with us,
But take us as your kindred,
And gladly set us free,
To ride across the desert lands,
The precious inheritance you have spared.
The noble hero will find his brave lion, they say,
And neighboring clans will camp together, they say,
And one rule will prevail in one land, they say,
So we bow our necks in submission.
He will look upon us with favor, they say,
And take us into his realm, they say;
Descendant of the noble hero,
We stand ready to become your inheritance.
Heed the words I have spoken;
I shall become your inheritance.
We know that your mighty presence
Can crush all who oppose you.
However much you spend, we are an inexhaustible
Mine of gold adornments;
Hero, if you lead us, we are your strength.
If you look closely and inquire,
The people behind you are your inheritance.
Turn and heed my words, brave lion:
All these people standing here,
If you spare them from death,
Will henceforth belong to you.
Understand these words of counsel;
Heed my words, noble lion.
If you tend this nation well,
We are falcons with collars,
We are steeds already saddled;
We shall stand as your support
And drive away your foes.
We shall strike the enemy without tiring;
Like sheltering boughs and branches,
We are plane trees in the barren waste.
For you, the hero who has come upon us,
We are a thousandfold inheritance you need.
We are the finest booty to fall into your hands,
One people among the Kalmyks;
We are the bright day of fortune
Granted to mortal man.
We are the stake to which you tether your horse;
Hero, if you keep us, we are your sustenance.
If you temper your mind and ponder deeply,
If you are truly a wise hero,
Descendant of the brave lion,
If you are the hero Seytek,
